kicker: Focus · Palestine: Gaza and the occupied West Bank
title: Palestine: Gaza and the West Bank
seo_title: Palestine: Gaza ceasefire deaths, winter floods, West Bank raids
dek: A year into the October 2025 ceasefire, Gaza's health ministry counts more than 1,500 killed since the truce; storms flood tent camps, and West Bank settler attacks hit a record.

summary.label: What's happening
summary.text: Despite an October 2025 ceasefire, Israeli strikes and fire still kill Palestinians in Gaza almost daily, health officials say.

summary.label: Why it matters
summary.text: About 950,000 displaced Gazans live in tents at flood risk; West Bank settler attacks hit a record in October.

summary.label: What's next
summary.text: Israel says reconstruction materials stay out until Hamas disarms; aid groups say shelter supplies are blocked as winter starts.

story.text: The war began when Hamas-led militants attacked southern Israel on 7 October 2023, killing some 1,200 people, mostly civilians, and taking 251 hostages. In Israel's offensive that followed, Gaza's health ministry says 74,640 Palestinians have been killed. The ministry, part of the Hamas-run government, does not separate civilians from combatants; the UN and many independent experts consider its figures the most reliable estimate.
story.takeaway: Two years of war killed about 1,200 people in Israel and, by Gaza's count, over 74,000 in Gaza.

story.text: A ceasefire began in October 2025. On 13 October 2025 all 20 living hostages were freed and Israel released more than 1,900 Palestinian prisoners. Killings in Gaza have continued: by 2 November 2026 the health ministry counted 1,593 people killed since the truce. Israel says many of those killed were Hamas fighters, often without giving evidence, Al Jazeera reports.
story.takeaway: The ceasefire freed the hostages, but deaths in Gaza continue.

story.text: Most of Gaza's people are displaced. The UN says about 950,000 live in sites at medium to high risk of flooding, entering a fourth winter in tents. The first storm of the season, on 7 November, flooded about 70,000 tents, Gaza's media office said. Aid groups blame Israeli limits on shelter materials; Israel rejects accusations that it restricts aid.
story.takeaway: Nearly a million people face winter in tents.
story.figcap: in tent sites at flood risk, UN says

story.text: In the occupied West Bank, OCHA documented 397 settler attacks causing casualties or damage in the first 26 days of October, the highest monthly figure since it began counting in 2006. Many hit the olive harvest. After masked settlers attacked European diplomats in Taybeh, police arrested 10 suspects; a court later released nine of them to house arrest.
story.takeaway: Settler attacks reached a record during the olive harvest.

story.text: After two Israeli soldiers were killed near Hebron on 23 October, Israel locked down the West Bank and began an operation in the city. About 5,000 people were displaced, Al Jazeera reported; Israel's defence minister said residents could not return until operations ended. The UN rights chief called it collective punishment and warned of "serious concerns of ethnic cleansing".
story.takeaway: Hebron's operation displaced thousands of Palestinians.

story.text: Two Israeli soldiers and two Palestinian gunmen were killed in an attack near Hebron. Israel ordered a full lockdown of the West Bank; Hebron's mayor said about 2,200 people were forced from their homes, while Israel's defence minister put it at about 2,000.

UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk said more than 3,000 Palestinians had been forced from their homes in Hebron, called it collective punishment and warned of "serious concerns of ethnic cleansing". No Israeli response to his statement was reported.

Gaza's health ministry put the toll since the ceasefire at 1,593. Hospitals said strikes on 1 November killed eight people, including five police officers in al-Mawasi; Israel's military said it struck military operatives.

The first winter storm flooded about 70,000 tents across Gaza, the Gaza media office said, with walls collapsing and people injured. The civil defence agency received about 1,500 distress calls in 10 hours. Aid groups blamed Israeli restrictions on shelter materials.

Israel released Palestinian journalist Abed Abou Shhadeh after five days in detention without charge on suspicion of "contact with a foreign agent". His lawyers at Adalah said police had no evidence; no official comment was reported.

Heavy rain collapsed a sandbank onto tents in Deir el-Balah, killing five people, four of them children, local health authorities said. Israeli security officials said 91,000 tents and tarps and 9,000 truckloads of clothes and blankets had entered for winter, and that reconstruction equipment and mobile homes would stay out while Hamas refuses to disarm.

A day after the Deir el-Balah landslide, two people were still missing, Al Jazeera reported. Save the Children said more than half a million children live in "critical or catastrophic" shelter conditions and that Israel has repeatedly blocked caravans the ceasefire promised; no Israeli response was reported.

official.text: Israel's military says its strikes in Gaza target Hamas fighters or "terrorists"; in many cases it gave no details. Israel rejects accusations that it restricts aid: security officials say 91,000 tents and tarps and 9,000 truckloads of winter supplies have entered, and that reconstruction equipment and mobile homes will not be allowed in while Hamas refuses to disarm. In Hebron, the military says it is dismantling "terrorist infrastructure", and the defence minister said residents cannot return until operations end. The military called the attack on diplomats in Taybeh "severe". No Israeli response to the UN rights chief's warning was reported.
points: Israel's military says its strikes in Gaza target Hamas fighters or "terrorists"; in many cases it gave no details or evidence.
Israel rejects accusations that it restricts aid; security officials say 91,000 tents and tarps and 9,000 truckloads of winter supplies have entered.
Reconstruction equipment and mobile homes will stay out while Hamas refuses to disarm, Israeli security officials say.
In Hebron the military says it is dismantling "terrorist infrastructure"; the defence minister said residents cannot return until operations end.
The military called the settler attack on diplomats in Taybeh "severe"; police arrested 10 suspects.
No Israeli response to the UN rights chief's ethnic-cleansing warning was reported.

whats_new.text: Two people were still missing after the Deir el-Balah landslide. Save the Children says Israel has blocked caravans the ceasefire promised; no Israeli response was reported.
